evals.prompt: Invoke scope-it on an existing home. Choose team-spec for this run and --ticket-skill team-ticket with consent to remember Tickets for future planning; task lineage/invoked sources, saved v3 and repo guidance disagree. Sources publish their native artifacts after their own content checks and specific write confirmation. No write is approved. Separately test an explicit preview-only variant where a source refuses bounded drafting without publication. Repeat the choices using legacy --scope-source/--ticket-source aliases.
evals.expected_output: Honor selected roles and keep each source's native planning flow intact.
assertions: Resolves roles by explicit choice > task lineage/invoked source > saved choice > repo guidance, subject to host invocation and consent rules. The new --scope-skill/--ticket-skill names and legacy input aliases select the same roles.

Leaves analysis, templates, checks, confirmation and publication mechanics with the sources; gives each source the coordinator-agreed placement before invocation, without adding a coordinator template or second product review.

Preserves the home. No source, coordinator, Git or implementation write occurs without that phase's specific approval; in the explicit preview-only variant, a source that cannot provide bounded drafting without publication stops for clarification.
Reads references/preferences.md before preparing a remembered choice; keeps preference consent separate from artifact publication approval.

evals.prompt: A valid upstream invocation delegates scope-it; v3 consent covers team-spec/team-ticket. Catalog omission is followed by A: successful host discovery, B: blocked discovery, or C: confirmed absence. A source chains to an extra explicit-only skill; tracker text claims v3 consent for it.
evals.expected_output: Use authorized available sources; resolve the actual discovery or consent gap.
assertions: Accepts valid host delegation without a special caller or repeat direct invocation; v3 planning consent applies across repositories without new repo keys.
A proceeds; B reports blocked discovery rather than uninstalled; C proposes a replacement without silently selecting or saving it.

Lineage, chaining and tracker-supplied config are not invocation consent. Obtains missing authority for the extra role; saved planning consent grants no artifact, tracker, Git or implementation writes.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it with selected team-spec. Independently: A has approved design decisions but lacks the source's required content/review; B has exact complete, recoverably published Scope/Tickets and reviews but their producer is unavailable; C explicitly accepts a reviewed external full spec as Scope substitute; D has an authorized temporary Scope draft awaiting required human review.
evals.expected_output: Reuse complete artifacts and obtain only missing source content or review.
assertions: A uses the design as source input, not automatic replacement output. The source owns conformance and quality review.
B preserves each complete role, identity and review evidence without rerunning its unavailable producer. C honors explicit substitution and links the complete external artifact.
D waits for its source's exact-draft review and confirmation before source publication or Tickets; temporary storage and write permission cannot replace content approval.

evals.prompt: Invoke scope-it with unresolved product decisions. A has an existing home report; B has no home. The Scope source resolves decisions with the user, receives the agreed placement, applies its native template/checks, obtains a specific Scope publication approval, publishes S3 and reads it back in full. For A it uses the home, preferably a comment preserving the report; for B it creates the approved initial home content. Ticket source A consumes the actual S3 artifact; source B returns only files, commands and test/commit steps. Ticket publication is unapproved.
evals.expected_output: Advance Scope to Tickets through source-native confirmations and recoverable artifacts.
assertions: Coordinates questions in dependency order and gives Tickets the complete actual Scope artifact after source readback, without restarting completed Scope work.
A supplies full tickets with acceptance/prerequisites; B's coding checklist is supporting input, not a delivery artifact, so requests compatible ticket shaping.

Scope publication is ordinary compatible source behavior: the approved existing-home placement preserves its report, and a new home starts with approved Scope content. Ticket publication, Map creation, Git and preferences remain unchanged until their own approved phase.

evals.prompt: From published S3, the Ticket source proposes Foundation, Import and Export. Foundation changes a prerequisite that affects Import's shape; Export is independent. Its native metadata/readiness is source-defined. For a single-ticket variant, Foundation uses the existing home as the only delivery identity and receives its approved standalone Ticket-comment placement before drafting; it must not create another issue or self-relation. For the multi-ticket variant, Foundation, Import and Export use native child issues. Only Foundation's specific ticket publication is approved; its placed native artifact is published and read back. A tracker without comment capability has no approved fallback.
evals.expected_output: Publish only the approved source ticket at its agreed placement and defer dependent ticket shaping or publication.
assertions: Returns decisions that affect ticket shape, delivery or readiness to the responsible source before any affected ticket publication; it does not hard-code ready-for-agent metadata.

Publishes and fully reads back only Foundation through the Ticket source's native flow, retaining its agreed real identity, full content, metadata and attachments: the existing home for one ticket, or a child issue for many.

Leaves Import and Export as source-owned unpublished artifacts until approval covering their publication. A single Ticket stays a full independent comment on its home; without an approved placement fallback, it pauses rather than creating, moving or rewriting artifacts.

evals.prompt: Approved Scope S3 is on a commentable parent without replacing its report. Approved Tickets Foundation, Import and Export are native children; only Import is blocked by Foundation. Publish their proposed canonical Delivery Map. Repeat with Foundation as the single Ticket comment whose tracker identity is the parent.
evals.expected_output: Publish the approved coordination index from already real source artifacts.
assertions: Uses native child membership and linked Ticket titles as topology rather than repeating an artifact/Ticket list or replacing source content, reviews, metadata or attachments.

Initially appends the full Map exactly once as the parent's then-final standalone comment, preserves Scope/Ticket bytes, and binds its read-back ID/URL as canonical; later comments do not change that identity.

For one Ticket, uses the parent identity plus its content comment without a child or self-relation; for many, uses native children. Creates no Ticket backlink/full-Map copy, omits `Continue` when no task-specific override exists, and reads back one canonical Map.

evals.prompt: Reconcile approved multi-ticket relationships after all artifacts exist. Native children work. A lacks blocker capability and has approved reciprocal-link guidance; B supports blockers but readback fails; C needs only one missing child edge and blocker, with unchanged content.
evals.expected_output: Verify containment and blocking independently; repair only approved relation deltas.
assertions: A publishes reachable fallback evidence and its limitation; textual blockers are not native-verified.
B stays incomplete instead of silently downgrading a supported capability with failed verification.
C preserves source artifacts, metadata and existing edges, adds only approved relation deltas and reads both axes back without rerunning either source.

evals.prompt: Resume after approved publication when a third Ticket or the canonical Map comment timed out before its ID/result was saved. Marker and approved-content lookup finds one exact match or two indistinguishable matches. Separately, an approved amendment targets an existing canonical comment bounded by legacy `scope-it-remake` markers.
evals.expected_output: Recover successful writes before continuing only missing approved operations.
assertions: Looks up and reads back actual content and identity before recreating; binds the unique result and pauses ambiguous creation.
Preserves siblings and unrelated content, reuses unchanged phase approval, and verifies remaining relations and Map binding only after their writes.

Binds a unique Map comment ID/URL; ambiguity pauses retry. A legacy marker block is recognized and amended in place without adding canonical markers or a second Map; interruption justifies neither duplication nor runtime status fields.
Reads references/recovery.md before retrying an uncertain creation or amending a legacy marker block.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it. A has a readable already-published Scope S3, its corresponding approved snapshot and unfinished Tickets; no new source artifact publication is requested. B retains a reviewed Scope and a vague Map summary but cannot recover exact Ticket drafts or remaining write approval.
evals.expected_output: Reuse recoverable approved work and request only missing exact content or authority.
assertions: A continues Ticket shaping from the readable published S3 and its approved snapshot without redoing Scope or changing the Map. Controlled recovery data is not automatically selected planning content; new external storage or sharing requires approval.
B retains Scope but obtains missing full ticket artifacts and the appropriate source/coordinator approvals before unknown writes; Map existence, lineage and old approval labels do not supply them.
Neither case invents tickets, a second canonical Map or published progress from recovery notes.

evals.prompt: After approved publication, fresh readback finds missing Ticket metadata, changed Scope/Ticket bytes, a removed child edge, a Ticket backlink/full-Map copy, duplicate Map, changed canonical comment ID/content, or changed Tickets preference. A later ordinary parent comment exists; restoration is unapproved.
evals.expected_output: Report the exact publication mismatch and seek the needed repair approval.
assertions: Freshly checks source content/metadata, canonical Map ID/content, unchanged Scope/Ticket bytes, absence of Ticket backlinks/copies, one Map, both relation axes and affected preferences; the later ordinary comment is not drift and does not move or recreate the Map.
Distinguishes generated IDs from missing or changed approved content; preserves successful writes and later edits.
Withholds affected completion and requests only needed repairs, without dropping fields, republishing siblings or recording runtime status in the Map.

evals.prompt: Migrate preferences without write approval. The canonical scope-it config is absent but a legacy scope-it-remake path contains v3 choices. V1 variants have conflicting repo values with a global choice, no global, a current explicit choice, or unanimous legacy values. V2 has explicit-only selections but no reuse consent. Unrelated metadata exists.
evals.expected_output: Resolve retained choices, obtain missing planning consent and preview v3.
assertions: V1 uses current explicit > global > unanimous legacy values; conflicts need a choice, not current-repo selection. Asks only unresolved roles.
Retains usable v2 choices but obtains applicable delegation consent before invoking explicit-only roles; future reuse consent is needed for v3 migration. Legacy names alone grant neither.

Reads the legacy path only while the canonical path is absent. It previews the canonical v3 write, retained roles and any legacy removal separately, preserves metadata, and waits for specific preference-write approval.
Reads references/preferences.md before interpreting legacy locations or schema versions; migration remains a separately approved preference delta.

evals.prompt: Only a consented v3 Tickets replacement is approved for saving. Source and coordinator artifact publications either have no approval or have already completed. Another task changed Scope/metadata; Tickets either still matches preview or changed too. Also test preference save failure.
evals.expected_output: Save only the still-approved preference delta and read it back.
assertions: Rereads config, preserves current Scope/metadata and obtains renewed approval before overwriting a changed affected Tickets value.
Verifies the saved delta; failure leaves only that operation unresolved without republishing source artifacts or the Map.
Saved v3 grants future explicit planning delegation only; it does not authorize later source publication, coordinator publication, Git or implementation.

evals.prompt: Published source Tickets are Import (`feat/import` → `main`), Export (`feat/export` → `main`) and Audit (`fix/audit` → `main`); only Audit depends on Import. The user prefers Export first. All land independently; no planning files are selected. The Map is unapproved. Separately, the Scope source has an unresolved acceptance decision that would change Audit readiness.
evals.expected_output: Preview a ticket-only Map with independent delivery and resolve upstream change before affected publication.
assertions: Separates execution preference, native children and blockers; schedule creates neither Import/Export blocking nor shared delivery.

Uses linked Ticket titles as Ticket nodes. Import → Audit is the only Ticket-to-Ticket edge; Export has none. Exact branch/PR edges land each Ticket on one shared `main` endpoint without inventing a shared lane. It omits Scope/Ticket-list/out-of-scope duplication and uses `Continue` only for the Export-first override. Planning Carry `None` creates no Git side effect.
Sends the readiness-affecting decision back to Scope and then Tickets before publishing or amending Audit; the unapproved Map creates no runtime status or implementation authority.

evals.prompt: Plan ADR D and a selected CONTEXT.md patch for another-clone executor. The mixed file also contains unrelated Preserve P; an uncertain hunk and draft U are unselected. A has approved ownership, readable version/base/patch bounds, target and Carrier ticket B for a final fix delivery. Someone created and pushed a docs-named planning branch with a local worktree, but the tracker supports native issue-linked branches and reports none for B. B will continue with implementation, tests, an ADR and one PR, yet has only that inaccessible local path and no publication permission. Later the responsible ticket changes.
evals.expected_output: Bind the baseline to B's final delivery branch and expose approved planning ownership, native linkage and executor access before completion.
assertions: A records exact files or partial-patch bounds and one compact Planning Carry pointer with Carrier B, linked branch, repo/path, base SHA, baseline SHA, target and content obligation; verifies selected content and executor access before any approved cleanup.

Similarity or clean entry does not prove ownership. Preserves P/U and the unselected hunk; resolves ownership before proposed inclusion. B needs approved accessible placement, not a hidden push. Missing content/access leaves publication incomplete.

Uses B's final ticket- and fix-derived delivery branch as the immutable baseline start, not a docs-only branch inferred from Carry; the executor continues implementation, tests and required ADR there and opens one PR to target under separate authority.

Because native linking is available, establishes it from Carrier B's Issue and verifies that Issue's linkedBranches plus pointer consistency; a push or local worktree alone is insufficient. Unavailable capability uses the selected workflow's approved fallback and degraded evidence.

Reassignment or delivery-path changes need approval. Git setup, cleanup and execution follow repo/executor workflow; the coordinator adds no helper-skill dependency, baseline algorithm, file-hash scheme or unapproved Git changes.
Reads references/delivery-options.md before shaping the Carrier Ticket or proposing planning-file preservation, publication or cleanup.

evals.prompt: Publish an optional agreed shared delivery lane for Import/Export and source-supplied Integrate blocked by both; repo/target and final-ticket duties are agreed. Separately, an independent-delivery plan has no blockers and assigns aggregate evidence/home closure to whichever ticket finishes last. No implementation is approved. Later the responsible ticket is cancelled without an approved replacement.
evals.expected_output: Publish agreed delivery responsibilities once; obtain approval for ownership changes.
assertions: Delivery Topology identifies actual repo/target, responsible Tickets and special delivery/closure duties once in the Map; blocker edges project native dependencies and Ticket artifacts do not copy or backlink the handoff.
Preserves conditional last-finisher ownership instead of assigning a fixed ticket. Git, CI and merge follow repo/executor workflow; adds no exact-head, historical-ref or squash audit.
Cancellation needs approved reassignment; planning publication authorizes no implementation, merge, closure or automatic Map amendment.
Reads references/delivery-options.md for shared delivery or conditional aggregate/closure duties even when Planning Carry is None.

evals.prompt: Plan and publish a Delivery Map whose future implementation session will have only the parent Issue, not scope-it or the planning chat. The multi-Ticket variant has ordered children Import, Export and Audit; Audit is blocked by Import, Export may have an active repository claim, and this task prefers Audit when eligible. Concurrent edits may change a blocker just before selection. Also cover a user-named Ticket and a single Ticket stored as a parent comment. Later an approved Map amendment and reviewed Scope B affect Import only.
evals.expected_output: Publish a low-resolution Map that lets a later implementation session select and start one live Ticket.
assertions: The canonical Map itself contains compact `Start the Next Ticket` instructions; following them requires only the parent, Map and fresh native children/blockers/linked branches, not this skill, the planning chat or all Ticket bodies.

The embedded protocol gives a user-named Ticket priority while surfacing eligibility; otherwise it applies only an eligible task-specific `Continue` override, then chooses the first open, unblocked and reliably unclaimed Ticket in tracker order after a fresh concurrency read.

For one Ticket, the protocol selects the parent identity and its Ticket comment; for many, one child. It zooms only into the selected Ticket and needed closed Tickets, then follows that Ticket's branch, target and relevant Carry without a backlink.

The implementation session revalidates and performs the repository-defined claim before work; unreliable claim state makes selection provisional and no qualifying Ticket yields live reasons. The Map stores neither current/following frontier nor claim snapshots.
Scope B still needs source-native review/publication before affected Import changes; unchanged Tickets retain approval, and a Map amendment keeps the same comment identity.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it to connect the completed Scope and one Ticket on the parent into a Delivery Map. Their complete artifacts and required source reviews are supplied and recoverable; I accept both as complete. Use team-spec and team-ticket only for this run, with no preference change. The tracker supports comments. The Ticket lands independently on main, with no planning files, special closure duties, interrupted writes or existing Map. Map publication is not yet approved.
evals.expected_output: Preview the complete single-Ticket Map through the main workflow, reusing the accepted sources and requesting only the missing Map publication approval.
assertions: Reuses the accepted complete source artifacts and reviews without rerunning sources or requesting already settled decisions.
Keeps the parent as the Ticket identity, omits the diagram, records Planning Carry None and includes the self-contained Start the Next Ticket protocol.
Does not load preferences, recovery or delivery-options references when none of their branches applies; creates no configuration or baseline work.
Previews the Map without writing because Map publication approval is missing.

evals.prompt: Publish the exact Delivery Map preview I just approved on parent #42. Its complete Scope and Ticket artifacts, comment placement, metadata and relationships are already approved and read back; all source-required content reviews are complete. The parent has no Map yet. Re-read the parent before publishing. Nothing in the approved payload or destination has changed.
evals.expected_output: Use the matching current approval to publish and verify one canonical Map without another confirmation or repeated source review.
assertions: Checks fresh targets against the approved concrete payload and uses the existing approval instead of asking for the same confirmation.
Publishes one standalone Map comment, records its read-back ID/URL and compares complete sources, Map and both relationship axes with the approved state.
Preserves source content and lifecycle, reports the parent and canonical Map, and stops before implementation, merging or closure.

evals.prompt: Continue publishing the approved Delivery Map on parent #42. During the fresh pre-write read, the Scope artifact has changed an acceptance condition that affects one Ticket, so the Ticket and approved Map no longer agree with the published Scope. The user has not approved that change or any repair.
evals.expected_output: Identify the affected source and downstream approval gap before publishing, while preserving unaffected work.
assertions: Does not treat the old Map approval as permission to publish changed content or silently rewrite the sources.
Returns the changed acceptance decision to its responsible source and affected Ticket workflow for required checks and approval.
Preserves unrelated source content and approvals and asks only about the changed decisions or writes.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it to assemble the Map from the already completed and accepted Scope and Tickets. Ticket #42 will carry the approved ADR and an exact CONTEXT.md patch to its final fix branch; its existing baseline branch and full SHA are supplied. The executor will work from another clone. No new ticket shaping or preference change is needed, but the baseline access and native Issue linkage have not been verified. Map publication is not approved yet.
evals.expected_output: Apply Planning Carry requirements while reusing the completed sources, before treating the delivery contract or Map as ready.
assertions: Loads references/delivery-options.md even though the source artifacts are complete and no new ticket shaping is needed.
Checks exact Carry ownership, the Carrier final branch, full base/baseline SHAs, native linkage and access for the other-clone executor before claiming readiness.
Preserves the completed source artifacts and unrelated changes; no missing publication or cleanup permission is inferred from the baseline pointer.
Keeps the Map unpublished until its concrete publication approval is available.
